task_goal: Unify four satisfaction variables to a common 1-5 scale, apply robust Z-score standardization, describe each distribution (mean/std/95% CI), and run one-way ANOVA (F, p, eta^2) across accommodation / indoor attractions / outdoor attractions / destination.

data_sources.notes: Listing-level review rating; 326 missing. Uniform-ish across 1-5 (mean 3.28), least negatively skewed of the four sources. Other columns (price, host info) not needed for satisfaction.

data_sources.file: FISETIO A FIne-grained, Structured and Enriched Tourism Dataset for Indoor and Outdoor attractions/datasets/indoors.csv
data_sources.notes: Monthly record per museum (date, museum, visits, weather, rating, revs, mus_ID); 254 distinct rating values, strongly left-skewed (skew -2.50) with a long lower tail down to 1.0.

data_sources.file: FISETIO A FIne-grained, Structured and Enriched Tourism Dataset for Indoor and Outdoor attractions/datasets/outdoors.csv
data_sources.notes: Monthly record per park (date, y, weather, rev, rate, park_id, park_name); 665 distinct values, truncated at a 3.0 floor (no 1-2 range), skew -1.44, very low dispersion (sd 0.26).

data_sources.role: tourists' satisfaction with the destination (transaction records)
data_sources.notes: Sheet 'Transaction' (dimension A1:G52931): TransactionId, UserId, VisitYear, VisitMonth, VisitMode, AttractionId, Rating. openpyxl unavailable in the environment, so the OOXML stream was parsed directly (sharedStrings + sheet1.xml); header mapping verified and rows persisted to tx_clean.csv. Rating skew -1.20.

steps: clip to [1,5]: values outside the common scale are winsorised onto the boundary
out-of-range values found: 0 in every source (all four variables already use a 1-5 metric, so no ratio rescaling is needed)
caveats: The four variables are not identical constructs: FISETIO rating/rate are venue-level aggregate ratings repeated over monthly rows, whereas Airbnb 'review rate number' and TripAdvisor 'Rating' are individual listing/transaction ratings. Repeated monthly aggregates make the effective FISETIO sample smaller than the row count and rows are not strictly independent.
outdoors 'rate' never drops below 3.0, so its 1-5 scale is de-facto truncated; central-tendency comparison is still valid on the common metric but dispersion is not comparable in raw units.

robust_standardization.formula: z = (x - median) / (1.4826 * MAD), MAD = median(|x - median|)
robust_standardization.note: Each source is centred on its own median and rescaled by its own robust spread: z=0 is that domain's typical (median) value, 1 unit = 1 robust SD of that domain.

standardized_source_statistics.note: identical to output1.csv; CI = mean +/- t(0.975, n-1) * sd/sqrt(n)

anova.test: one-way ANOVA (scipy.stats.f_oneway) on the robust-standardized values
anova.p_value_note: p underflows IEEE-754 double precision (scipy returns 0.0). Asymptotic evaluation of the F upper tail (log I_y(df2/2, df1/2) with y = df1*F/(df2+df1*F)) gives log10(p) ~ -137512, i.e. p < 1e-300: the equal-means null is rejected by an enormous margin.
anova.effect_size_interpretation: eta^2 = 0.019 => ~1.9% of total variance in standardized scores lies between domains: statistically decisive but practically small.

anova_on_raw_1to5_values.note: Robust-z changes the ranking: in raw 1-5 units accommodation (3.28) has the lowest mean and outdoor (4.67)/indoor (4.38) the highest (eta^2=0.127), while after per-source robust centring the ordering reflects how far each mean sits from its own median (accommodation +0.19, destination +0.11, outdoor -0.19, indoor -0.65) and eta^2 shrinks to 0.019. Both reject equality, so the qualitative conclusion (systematic differences exist) is robust to the scoring choice.

sanity_checks.excel_parse_validation: OOXML stream parse reproduced the declared sheet dimension A1:G52931 (52930 data rows); header/column mapping confirmed against sharedStrings; all 7 columns numeric, 0 missing.
sanity_checks.no_out_of_range_values: min/max of every source already lie inside [1,5]; clipping changed no observation.

key_findings: All four domains share a 1-5 satisfaction metric but differ sharply in shape/spread: Airbnb ratings are near-uniform (sd 1.28, median 3), TripAdvisor destination ratings pile up at 4-5 (sd 0.97), indoor museum ratings are tightly bunched high (median 4.55, sd 0.56, long lower tail to 1.0), outdoor park ratings are the highest and tightest (median 4.71, sd 0.26, floor 3.0).

After robust centring every 95% CI of the standardized means excludes 0 and no two CIs overlap: accommodation +0.188 [0.183, 0.194], destination +0.106 [0.101, 0.112], outdoor -0.189 [-0.229, -0.148], indoor -0.650 [-0.730, -0.571].

One-way ANOVA: F(3, 160798) = 1064.89, p < 1e-300 (double 0.0), eta^2 = 0.019 - domain means differ significantly, but the effect size is small because within-domain variance (dominated by the huge Airbnb and TripAdvisor samples) is large.
Post-hoc Welch tests: all six pairwise contrasts are significant (all p < 1e-20); largest separation accommodation vs indoor attractions (d = 0.52), smallest accommodation vs destination (d = 0.11).

Interpretation caveats: the very large N (160,798) inflates significance, and venue-level aggregates (FISETIO) are compared with individual-level ratings. Practically, indoor cultural attractions show the most left-skewed / lower-tail-heavy satisfaction profile while outdoor venues show the most uniformly high ratings.
